result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A ties more of its choices to how Clutchpoint is used: glare at the roadside, one thumb, weak signal, and a diary or logbook for reference. It keeps the driving motif to a single 'bite point' notch and points out its own assumptions about payment and offline saving. Answer B gives slightly more exact values, such as border widths, spacing and motion timing, and adds useful process steps. However, it leans harder on the road-sign look with uppercase labels and a hard offset shadow, and it assumes lesson length and price appear in booking slots. Neither answer gives a system font fallback. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both briefs share a strong core: a warm paper background, near-black ink and one amber or yellow accent, ruled rows instead of cards, a bottom action bar within thumb reach, one-tap Mark done with Undo, and offline saving. B ties its choices more closely to how instructors actually work, for example showing last lesson's notes and changing the main action from Start to Mark done to Take payment. It keeps the driving motif light by using the bite-point notch in one place only, bans invented stats and sample data, and tells the user which assumptions to check. A is tighter and very pasteable, but it uses all-caps labels and a hard offset shadow, and its ban list pairs fewer items with alternatives. Neither brief gives system font fallbacks, and B mislabels the 7:1 contrast ratio as WCAG AA when it is the AAA level.
